svg.aria-label: clowk architecture: inbound capture at the paste boundary, a broker daemon holding real values in memory, and three delivery tiers that apply a credential at the moment of use
svg.title: clowk — architecture
svg.text: clowk
the agent never holds a usable credential — it holds a reference, and a local broker applies the real value at the moment of use
real value
reference only
clowk component
blocked
A — INBOUND · CATCH IT AT THE PASTE BOUNDARY (verified live, unchanged)
YOU PASTE
sk_live_4eC39Hq…
into the chat
nothing is sent yet
HOOK · LOCAL
UserPromptSubmit
220 gitleaks rules,
before anything is sent
ON A HIT
the turn is BLOCKED — the model gets
nothing, the transcript records nothing
the value goes to the broker, and a tier
is chosen for it
YOU GET BACK
your prompt, rewritten. Already on your
clipboard — repaste is one keystroke.
the only friction in the design, and unavoidable:
a hook can block a prompt but cannot rewrite one
THE BROKER · A PER-USER DAEMON · THE ONLY HOLDER OF REAL VALUES
values live in its memory · vault on disk is encrypted, key in the OS keychain
a unix socket at 0600 · auto-spawns on first use, no lifecycle to manage
its API is use-only. There is deliberately no call that returns a raw value.
ssh-agent's discipline: present a reference, the broker performs the operation, the key never leaves
B — OUTBOUND · APPLY THE VALUE AT THE MOMENT OF USE, THREE WAYS
one tier is chosen per secret automatically, and clowk list always says which — so the protection level is never ambiguous
T1 · NATIVE CREDENTIAL HOOKS
the tool asks; the broker answers
The ecosystem already standardised
"do not store it, ask a program".
git credential.helper=clowk
aws credential_process
docker credsStore
kubectl exec plugin
git is verified working today
Broker → tool, directly.
Never in env. Never in argv.
Never in a file the agent reads.
accident-proof, not adversary-proof: see below
T2 · LOCALHOST REVERSE PROXY
point the base URL at the broker
The agent's env holds a worthless
reference and a localhost URL:
OPENAI_API_KEY=clowk_ref_a1b2
OPENAI_BASE_URL=
plain localhost HTTP inbound; the broker
makes the real HTTPS call outbound
No HTTPS_PROXY. No TLS to
intercept. No CA to trust.
host binding is structural — a route only
reaches its own upstream, so a stolen
reference cannot be aimed elsewhere
T3 · SCOPED INJECTION · LAST RESORT
one child process, one command
For tools with neither a credential
hook nor a configurable endpoint.
clowk run -- ./deploy.sh
real value in that one child's env,
output scrubbed, use logged
explicit and narrow — clowk is never in
the path of ls, a build, or a test run
Forget to use it and the reference
yields a 401 that says what to do:
it fails closed and self-corrects.
so nothing here needs an unverified hook API
WHAT THIS STOPS
a pasted key reaching the model, the transcript, or disk
env or printenv — the agent's environment holds references
a reference being aimed at a host it does not belong to
a stolen reference being worth anything off this machine
git credential fill and friends — now on the deny list
that last one printed a live token during this design session
WHAT IT DOES NOT
T1: a deliberate agent can invoke the helper itself
T3: the value is in one child's env and argv while it runs
a file you @-mention — the host reads that, not clowk
Grep, and possibly subagent tool calls: host-side reads
a credential in a format the 220 rules do not recognise
closing these needs OS sandboxing — the cost this design refuses
